newsitem.title: USA: FBI finds similarities between Atlanta bombings.
newsitem.headline: FBI finds similarities between Atlanta bombings.

text.p: The FBI said on Monday there were distinct similarities between the bomb that injured five people at a nightclub last weekend and last month's bombing of an abortion clinic but they had no substantiated links.

Investigators cautioned it was too early to conclude both attacks were the work of the same person or group, saying a federal crime lab had yet to issue forensic reports on the two bombs that exploded at the gay and lesbian nightclub.
"There are distinct similarities (in the composition of the bombs)," FBI spokesman Jay Spadafore told Reuters. "And, there are also some differences."

The FBI said on Saturday that the explosion at The Otherside Lounge in northeast Atlanta was similar enough to the abortion clinic bombing and last July's pipe bomb attack at Centennial Olympic Park for investigators to suspect that a serial bomber could be at work.

ABC News later said investigators had found striking similarities between the nightclub and abortion clinic bombings. It said components were "so similar" investigators believed the same person or group was responsible for both.
But authorities on Monday sought to play down reports of any conclusion about the bombers.

"At this point, we're not ruling out anything. That includes the possibility of a serial bomber and it includes the possibility of a copy-cat bomber," Atlanta Police Chief Beverly Harvard said on a radio news programme.

Federal officials said no conclusion could be reached until investigators had ended their search of the bomb site. "That conclusion has not yet been reached, contrary to reports you may have seen," Spadafore said.

"For one thing, we haven't gotten results back on this bomb. We've not even finished the crime scene yet, so we'd really be jumping the gun making that determination before we finish the crime scene here."

The nightclub bomb, apparently packed with nails, went off in the rear patio section of the lounge shortly before 10 p.m. EST on Friday. Staff said the club, one of Atlanta's few predominantly lesbian bars, was about half full at the time.
Police found a second bomb in a backpack hidden among some bushes in an adjacent parking lot and detonated the device with a remote-control robot.
Most injuries were slight. But one woman had to have surgery to remove shrapnel from her right shoulder. She was later listed in stable condition.
Both police and nightclub staff said there were no prior warnings and no claims of responsibility for the attack.
